title: Actionable error recovery
summary: Error states should explain what failed, preserve recoverable user input, and provide the clearest next action rather than merely announcing failure.
problem: Generic error messages leave users without a recovery path and often cause repeated work or data loss.
use_when: Forms, uploads, authentication, payments, saves, sync, network requests, and destructive actions can fail
A user may need to correct input or retry an operation
avoid_when: The system can transparently recover without interrupting the user
A transient non-critical event does not require user action
rationale: A failure message is useful only when the user can understand the consequence and next step.
Preserving valid input reduces repeated work.
Inline errors are usually more actionable when the problem belongs to a specific field or control.

requirements: Preserve valid user-entered data where safe.
Associate field-specific errors with the relevant control.
Offer retry or correction when the user can resolve the failure.
Do not expose internal stack traces or implementation details.
